solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Superstar singer Celine rather dim, as it turns out

indicators.note: something that turns out differently has been changed round, so the letters before it come out in a new order

blocks.note: fifteen letters of fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: A jibe at Celine Dion, implying the famous singer is not very bright.
explanation.walkthrough: Celine Dion is a real superstar singer, so the eye takes her as the subject; her name is just letters to rearrange into MARLENE DIETRICH.
explanation.definitionFit: The German-born film star was also a celebrated cabaret performer, famous for recordings such as Lili Marleen.

clue.text: Crazy time after necking island wine that’s quite potent

indicators.note: to neck something is to swallow it down, so one piece takes another inside itself

blocks.note: crazy is mad
an era is a period of time
I is the standard abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: A wild evening of knocking back strong wine on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' just places the time piece after the crazy piece. Madeira is itself an island, which makes the island in the wordplay a neat double bluff.
explanation.definitionFit: Madeira is a fortified wine, strengthened with grape spirit, so it is stronger than ordinary table wine.

clue.text: Fanatical bishop detained by police operation

indicators.note: someone detained is held inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
a raid is a police swoop on premises

explanation.surface: A zealous churchman is picked up during a police swoop.
explanation.walkthrough: The bishop is a single letter held inside the operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid is used figuratively of extreme, unreasoning zeal, as in a rabid supporter or rabid fan.

clue.text: Starts to encourage good lad, soldier, popular base climber

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters, so only the first letter of each word is kept

blocks.note: the initial letters of the three words
a soldier ant is a kind of worker ant, so ant stands for soldier
in means fashionable or popular
e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: A sergeant urging a young recruit up a climbing wall from the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' looks like a mountaineer in a training scene, but it is a plant. E for base comes from maths, where e is the base of natural logarithms.
explanation.definitionFit: Eglantine is the sweet briar, a wild rose whose long arching stems scramble over hedges and walls.

clue.text: A touch of froideur as I approach huge land mass

indicators.note: a touch of something is only a small part of it, so the answer is a stretch of the letters that follow

blocks.note: letters running across the four words

explanation.surface: Someone senses a chill as they near a vast continent.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts inside the French word for coldness and ends with the first letter of the last word.
explanation.definitionFit: Eurasia is the single continental block formed by Europe and Asia together, the largest on Earth.

clue.text: Japanese art Nick put up in furniture store

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up lifts it so it reads from bottom to top
one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: to nick is to steal or nab
IKEA is the Swedish furniture retailer

explanation.surface: Someone called Nick hanging a Japanese print on display in a furniture shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick reads like a man's name, but it is the verb meaning steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ikebana is the traditional Japanese discipline of formal flower arranging.

clue.text: Delay attempt to cross a river

indicators.note: to cross something here is to straddle it, so the outer piece spans the inner letters

blocks.note: an attempt is a try
taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Holding up a river crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: The attempt surrounds the article and the river abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To tarry is an old-fashioned verb for lingering or staying longer than planned.

clue.text: Translate sign on sandwich shop south of Bury

definitions.note: a verb phrase: to interpret is to explain a sign's meaning

indicators.note: in a down clue, south of something means placed below it, so this piece follows the other

blocks.note: to inter is to bury
Pret A Manger is a British chain of sandwich shops

explanation.surface: Puzzling over a shop sign in the Lancashire town of Bury.
explanation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the town near Manchester, but it is the verb. Pret is the everyday name for the Pret A Manger chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Interpreting means rendering meaning from one form into another, whether a foreign language or signs and gestures.

clue.text: Blade kicks ace debutant for Wednesday

indicators.note: a debutant makes a first appearance, so only the first letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: to hack in football is to kick an opponent's legs
A is the card abbreviation for ace
the opening letter of the day

explanation.surface: A Sheffield United player fouls the star newcomer of local rivals Sheffield Wednesday.
explanation.walkthrough: The Blades is the nickname of Sheffield United and Wednesday is the rival Sheffield club, so the surface is a football derby; Blade is really the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacksaw is a saw with a thin fine-toothed steel cutting edge held in a frame.

clue.text: An occasional player, daughter more skilful potting black

indicators.note: potting a ball sends it into a pocket, so one piece is put inside another

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
abler means more capable
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A daughter outplays her father at snooker by sinking the black.
explanation.walkthrough: Snooker vocabulary makes the black look like the final ball; it is just its abbreviation, pocketed inside the skilful piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A dabbler takes part in an activity casually and superficially, without serious commitment.

clue.text: Best to leave triceratops running all over the place

indicators.note: what leaves is no longer there, so these letters are taken away
something running is in motion and disordered, so the remaining letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the tops means the very best
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dinosaur stampede, with the best of them leaving the scene.
explanation.walkthrough: The dinosaur's name ends conveniently in the letters for best; remove them and seven letters remain to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erratic is irregular and unpredictable, which matches the idiom for being chaotic and inconsistent.

clue.text: I’m formally visiting part of Asia, a majority Muslim land

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside someone else's place, so one piece enters another

blocks.note: one's, short for one is, is the formal impersonal way of saying I am
India is a country in southern Asia

explanation.surface: A formal traveller announces a visit to an Asian country with a Muslim majority.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is reading I'm in its stiff formal form, one's (one is), rather than as a pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: The archipelago nation has the world's largest Muslim population, so it qualifies as a predominantly Islamic country.

clue.text: Bowls over exhausted, covered by broadcaster from the east

indicators.note: something exhausted has been emptied out, so only the outer letters remain
in an across clue, reading from the east means right to left
what is covered sits under a wrapping, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
Sky is a British satellite broadcaster

explanation.surface: A tired bowler is caught on camera by a TV crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowls over' wants to be the definition, meaning knocks down; over is wordplay. In cricket, to york a batsman is to bowl a yorker, a ball pitched right at their feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Yorking is a cricket verb for delivering a full-length ball that lands near the batsman's toes.

clue.text: Coffee bar, laid back, in traffic-free Caribbean island

indicators.note: laid back literally means set down backwards, so the letters run the other way
free of traffic means with the jam gone, so those letters are removed
one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: taken as written
Jamaica is a large island in the Caribbean

explanation.surface: A relaxed coffee bar on a peaceful island with no cars.
explanation.walkthrough: Traffic-free here means the island loses JAM, as in a traffic jam, leaving AICA to hold the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabica is the main species of coffee plant, and its beans make most of the coffee people drink.

clue.text: Love goddess received hairstyle colouring before tea

indicators.note: what is received has been heard by a listener, so the words count by sound rather than spelling

blocks.note: an Afro hairstyle, dye for colouring, then tea

explanation.surface: A hairdresser's appointment: an Afro, a colour, then a cup of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: Received looks like 'got', but it means heard; say Afro, dye, tea in a row.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology she is the deity of love and beauty, the counterpart of the Roman Venus.

clue.text: RAF personnel broadcast war cries endlessly

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off
to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so these letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Air force men shouting battle cries over the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: Broadcast suggests a radio or a sound-alike; here it is scattering, as of seed.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircrew are the people who fly and operate an aircraft, such as pilots and gunners in the Royal Air Force.

clue.text: Rubbish side brings in wingers from relegated City

indicators.note: wingers play on the flanks, so only the outside letters are kept
bringing something in takes it inside, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: rot means nonsense or rubbish
a side is a team
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A poor football club, just relegated, signs wide players from a city rival.
explanation.walkthrough: City looks like part of a football club name such as Manchester City; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotterdam is the second-largest Dutch city and home to Europe's biggest seaport.

clue.text: Most sore area, source of infection in thorax

indicators.note: a source is where something starts, so only the first letter is kept
one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area
the thorax is the chest
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A doctor locating the most painful spot of a chest infection.
explanation.walkthrough: The medical surface makes the whole clue sound like a diagnosis; the chest is a piece that takes in one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Achiest is the superlative of achy, describing the place that hurts with the strongest dull pain.

clue.text: Pleasant introduction to amusing, fine tale

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so only the first letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
a fable is a moral tale

explanation.surface: A storyteller praised for the nice opening of a funny story.
explanation.walkthrough: Fine gives F as on pencils and fishing lines; the tale is a fable.
explanation.definitionFit: Affable describes a person who is friendly, good-natured and easy to talk to.

clue.text: Join the group after dropping new language

indicators.note: once something is dropped it is left behind, so this letter is removed

blocks.note: to tag along is to go with a group
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Advice to a newcomer about fitting in with a group.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the N from the phrasal verb leaves the name of the language.
explanation.definitionFit: Tagalog is the Austronesian tongue of the central Philippines and the basis of Filipino, its national standard.

clue.text: Rhetorical device T S Eliot exploited

indicators.note: something exploited has been worked over and used, so the letters are reworked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic says the poet made full use of a figure of speech.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet's name with initials supplies exactly the seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Litotes is understatement by denying the opposite, as in 'not bad' meaning good, a classic figure of speech.

clue.text: Cross family butler filmed very naked

indicators.note: stripped naked means the outer covering is gone, so only the inner letters remain

blocks.note: Lurch is the butler in the Addams Family films
the two inner letters

explanation.surface: An annoyed butler caught on camera wearing nothing at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross looks like angry; it is a noun for a cross-bred dog. Lurch is the tall butler in The Addams Family.
explanation.definitionFit: A lurcher is a dog bred from a sighthound mated with a working breed such as a collie or terrier.

clue.text: Terrorist agents respect regional borders

indicators.note: the words placed either side form borders around a run of letters inside them

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Militants who honour the boundaries of local regions.
explanation.walkthrough: The run starts inside the first word and ends at the start of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: In the James Bond stories, SPECTRE is the criminal organisation of spies and saboteurs led by Blofeld.

clue.text: Jeer at loud yobbo

blocks.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
a yobbo is a lout, a British slang word for an uncouth young man

explanation.surface: Mocking a noisy thug.
explanation.walkthrough: Loud is a musical marking abbreviated to F, for forte.
explanation.definitionFit: The older sense of flout is to mock or scoff at openly, showing contempt.

clue.text: African boy king is getting upset

indicators.note: upset means turned over, and in a down clue that flips the letters upward

blocks.note: Tutankhamun, Egypt's boy king, is often called King Tut
taken as written

explanation.surface: A young king becoming distressed.
explanation.walkthrough: Upset reads as distressed but it flips the short word over.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tutsi are an ethnic group of Rwanda and Burundi in central Africa, so a Tutsi is an African person.

clue.text: Fed up hanging around in Paris station’s old toilet

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the letters run backwards
one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: fed up means bored
gare is French for a railway station

explanation.surface: A weary traveller loitering in a Paris railway station's old lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: Hanging around reads as loitering, but it turns the fed-up piece round.
explanation.definitionFit: A garderobe was a medieval castle privy, often a small chamber jutting from the wall over a drop.

clue.text: Regularly tout Bangkok, an area popular with tourists

indicators.note: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A street hawker in the Thai capital touting for tourist business.
explanation.walkthrough: Bangkok suggests the answer is in Thailand, but the area is in New Zealand.
explanation.definitionFit: Otago is a region of New Zealand's South Island, home to Queenstown, a major destination for visitors.

clue.text: Brother discovered guns in port

indicators.note: dis-covered means with its cover removed, so the outside letters go and the inner ones remain

blocks.note: Br is the abbreviation for brother
guns are pistols, and this keeps its inner letters

explanation.surface: A monk caught smuggling firearms through a harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: Discovered reads as found out, but it means uncovered: the guns lose their first and last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Bristol is a city in south-west England with a long history as a major harbour and trading port.

clue.text: RLS character’s unfinished diatribe, the source of an outpouring in the street

definitions.text: the source of an outpouring in the street

indicators.note: something unfinished lacks its end, so the last letter is cut off

blocks.note: Mr Hyde is the alter ego in Robert Louis Stevenson's novella
a diatribe is a rant

explanation.surface: A villain's angry speech is cut short as he harangues passers-by in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: RLS is Robert Louis Stevenson; outpouring hints at the rant but describes water.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire hydrant is a street-side water outlet that gushes when opened for fire crews.

clue.text: One pressed for oil governs in empire that’s in disorder

indicators.note: things in disorder are jumbled, so these letters are mixed into a new order

blocks.note: fifteen letters of fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: An oil-hungry ruler presiding over a crumbling empire.
explanation.walkthrough: One pressed for oil sounds like a nation squeezed for petroleum; it is a plant whose seeds are pressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeds of this yellow-flowered plant are crushed to make a popular herbal supplement sold in capsules.
